modules.title: Application Layer & Protocol Layering
modules.description: HTTP, FTP, e-mail (SMTP/IMAP), DNS, and P2P architectures.

HTTP protocol, persistent connections & cookies
Domain Name System (DNS) resolution & record types
Electronic mail architecture (SMTP, POP3, IMAP)
Peer-to-Peer file distribution (BitTorrent, DHT)

modules.description: Transport layer (UDP, TCP) + sockets hands-on; Network layer (routing, multicast, IPv6, QoS).

TCP connection management, flow control (sliding window)
TCP congestion control (AIMD, Slow Start, Fast Recovery)
Socket programming API fundamentals

IPv6 addressing, multicast & QoS principles

Multiple Access protocols: CSMA/CD and CSMA/CA
Ethernet standard framing & MAC addressing
Wireless LAN IEEE 802.11 architecture

Signal impairment: Attenuation, distortion, Nyquist/Shannon capacity
Digital transmission: Line coding (NRZ, Manchester, AMI)
Network Management: SNMP architecture & MIB structure
ASN.1 basic encoding rules

modules.description: Analysis, asymptotics, recurrences (Master theorem), AVL trees.

Recurrence relations: Substitution & Recursion Tree
Master Theorem all 3 cases with boundary conditions
AVL Tree rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL) & rebalancing

Graph traversals: BFS & DFS classification of edges
Strongly Connected Components (Kosaraju & Tarjan)

Divide and conquer: Strassen matrix multiplication analysis

Dijkstra's Single Source Shortest Path with priority queues

All-pairs shortest paths: Floyd-Warshall algorithm

Complexity classes P, NP, NP-Hard, and NP-Complete
Polynomial time reductions (Circuit-SAT to 3-SAT)
Vertex Cover & Clique NP-completeness proofs

Polynomial representation and addition using lists

notes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms (FCFS, SJF, RR) — KTU Notes
notes.content:
# CPU Scheduling Algorithms — KTU Examination Notes

KTU 7-Mark Model Answer & Numerical Reference
Operating Systems — Module 2

## 1. Core Scheduling Formulas
- Turnaround Time: TAT = CT - AT
- Waiting Time: WT = TAT - BT
- Average Waiting Time: AWT = (Σ WT) / N
- Average Turnaround Time: ATAT = (Σ TAT) / N

## 2. Algorithm Summary & Trade-offs
1. First Come First Serve (FCFS):
   - Non-preemptive, FIFO.
   - Suffers from Convoy Effect (short processes stuck behind long ones).
2. Shortest Job First (SJF):
   - Non-preemptive / Preemptive (SRTF).
   - Minimizes AWT; risk of Starvation for long processes.
3. Round Robin (RR):
   - Preemptive, time-sliced using Time Quantum.
   - Prevents starvation; performance sensitive to time quantum size.

## 3. KTU Valuation Marks Scheme (7 Marks)
1. Definitions & Objectives: 1 Mark
2. Working Principle: 1 Mark
3. Clear Gantt Chart: 2 Marks
4. Numerical Table (CT, TAT, WT) & AWT / ATAT: 2 Marks
5. Advantages, Disadvantages & Key Phenomena (Convoy/Starvation): 1 Mark

notes.title: Master Theorem Reference & Edge Cases
notes.content:
For recurrence T(n) = a*T(n/b) + f(n):
Compare f(n) with n^(log_b a):
1. If f(n) = O(n^(log_b a - ε)) for ε > 0, then T(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a)).
2. If f(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a) * log^k n) for k ≥ 0, then T(n) = Θ(n^(log_b a) * log^(k+1) n).
3. If f(n) = Ω(n^(log_b a + ε)) for ε > 0, and regularity condition a*f(n/b) ≤ c*f(n) holds for c < 1, then T(n) = Θ(f(n)).

*KTU Trap*: Watch out for polynomial vs polylogarithmic gaps where Master theorem does not apply!

notes.title: TCP Congestion Control & 3-Way Handshake
notes.content:
Three-way handshake:
1. Client -> Server: SYN (seq = x)
2. Server -> Client: SYN-ACK (seq = y, ack = x+1)
3. Client -> Server: ACK (ack = y+1)

Congestion Control States:
- Slow Start: cwnd starts at 1 MSS, doubles every RTT (exponential growth) until ssthresh.
- Congestion Avoidance: cwnd increases by 1 MSS per RTT (linear growth).
- Triple Duplicate ACK: Fast Retransmit + Fast Recovery (ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd = ssthresh + 3 MSS).
- Timeout: Severe drop: ssthresh = cwnd/2, cwnd resets to 1 MSS (re-enter Slow Start).

notes.title: ARM Cortex-M Stacks & Register Architecture
notes.content:
Core Registers:
- R0 - R12: General purpose registers
- R13: Stack Pointer (MSP for OS/Handler mode, PSP for Thread mode)
- R14: Link Register (LR) holds return address
- R15: Program Counter (PC)
- xPSR: Program Status Register (APSR, IPSR, EPSR)

NVIC features:
- 1 to 240 interrupts, nested vectoring with 8 to 256 priority levels.
- Hardware auto-stacking of R0-R3, R12, LR, PC, xPSR on exception entry in 12 clock cycles.
